techniques.name: Typed request, then the real result
techniques.description: Plain request typed in a field cropped so it fills about half the width (line box 9.4% of frame height), then 1-2 s of the agent's real log (hard cut onto it already scrolling, e.g. F278), then the real result in the software, each pass ending on a visible state change (22 items collapse into 4 folders about 13.44 s; a new track arrives about 21.0 s; generated close-ups flicker in the preview 32.60-32.84 s). Three passes, 4.4-7.7 s each.
techniques.routeReason: Recorded interface played with ScreenPlayback, framed with RegionCamera. The recording has to be real, so it depends on a working demo.

sound.note: Nothing established for the passes as a whole. audio.json holds 132 onsets in 39 s (about 3.4 a second), so an onset within 50 ms of any time is near chance (about a third); tempo confidence 0.074 rules out a beat grid.

techniques.name: Interface cropped so one action fills the frame
techniques.description: Hard jumps between crops of one recording, never a slow zoom: the field fills about half the width, the timeline is cut tighter in one frame (F459, 18.36 s: diff 23.5 on that frame, 0.0-0.2 either side). The eye is put on the one action that matters, at reading size.

sound.note: The crop cuts fall inside the 14.2-21.9 s stretch where loudness peaks pulse and 9 of 9 cuts land 0.01-0.06 s before a peak; that window was chosen after seeing the peaks, so it suggests and does not prove a method.

techniques.name: Output leaves its preview and fills the frame
techniques.description: The generated close-up appears in the small preview (F822, 32.88 s) and the preview grows at a steady rate (frame difference level at 15-23 a frame) until it fills the frame and the interface has gone (F834, 33.36 s, 0.48 s); the face then keeps pushing in slowly (diff 4-8) for 12 more frames before the burst cuts in at F847.
techniques.routeReason: GrowToScene (or LayoutMorph) over a screen recording; the footage inside must be swapped for the full-resolution asset as it grows.

sound.note: An onset at 32.879 s coincides with the preview appearing (F822); audio.json holds 132 onsets in 39 s (about 3.4 a second), so an onset within 50 ms of any time is near chance (about a third); tempo confidence 0.074 rules out a beat grid.

techniques.name: Camera pushes from a room into the screen
techniques.description: Real camera on a monitor, matched to a screen recording. In: the camera moves past the soft foreground bottle (F113-F118, 0.24 s) and pushes down into the monitor, decelerating, until the dock fills the frame and stops dead (F119-F130, 0.48 s). Out: from the flat interface the camera pulls back to the monitor in a dark room, accelerating over 1.0 s (F578-F603), cut short by a 3-frame fall to black. Quality is lost if rendered: real focus, reflections and hand-held drift.
techniques.routeReason: A real desk and monitor filmed by a person. Without a camera, nearest is a Blender monitor with the recording as a texture, which needs the user's approval, or a RegionCamera pull-back that drops the room.

sound.note: An onset at 4.481 s sits 39 ms before the push starts; audio.json holds 132 onsets in 39 s (about 3.4 a second), so an onset within 50 ms of any time is near chance (about a third); tempo confidence 0.074 rules out a beat grid.

techniques.name: The film's opening is the tool's output
techniques.description: The result preview plays material the viewer has already seen (the film's opening shot, with its typed caption), small in the editor at 21.4 s and then large, with a new caption appearing in the preview (23.12 s) before the pull-out. Works only if the tool really made it, otherwise it is a false claim.
techniques.routeReason: For a product that is not a video tool this does not transfer as such. Nearest equivalent: the product's real output, seen earlier in the film as an unexplained image, later revealed to come from it.

sound.note: Not established whether the preview's own sound plays.

techniques.name: Two-frame image burst with a fixed caption
techniques.description: 33 generated images held 2 frames each at 25 fps (0.08 s; three held 3 frames), each aligned so the eye sits at frame centre, closing in steadily from face to eye to pupil (pupil about 30% of width by F910) and ending on a crater that rhymes with the pupil, under one still caption at frame centre that never moves.
techniques.routeReason: Needs many images: generated ones need a budget; our own interface states or licensed stills could be used. The flurry block cuts a run of stills under a locked phrase; aligning each still on one feature is not built. Quality lost with few images: the sense of plenty.

sound.note: The burst sits on the densest, loudest stretch of the waveform (edit map 33.9-36.6 s); no single hit is tied to it and no beat grid can be trusted.

techniques.name: Short human reaction with one-word caption
techniques.description: Real person for 0.6-0.7 s between interface passages, a one- or two-word caption cut on with the shot (F354 and F371 single-frame changes, nothing moves between: diff 0.1-0.3), small, beside or between the eyes.
techniques.routeReason: A person acting. Generated would lose the credibility the passage exists to give.

sound.note: Both reaction cuts fall 50 ms before an onset (14.211, 28.491 s), inside the 14.2-21.9 s loudness pulse whose peaks the cuts lead by 0.01-0.06 s; that window was chosen after seeing the peaks, and onsets are dense, so this suggests and does not prove a method.

techniques.name: Doubt stated on black
techniques.description: White question on pure black, 0.9-1.5 s, before each proof. First variant (7.04-8.56 s): the line strobes for 12 frames between a full-frame stack of echoes and two copies at top and bottom (F176-F187, every frame changes), settles to one centred line (F187), is erased word by word from the left and rebuilt word by word from the right (F189-F201, a word every frame), holds 7 frames, dims and cuts to black for 2 frames before the next shot (F210-F213). Second variant: the line arrives over the monitor as it falls to black (F601-F603) and simply holds.
techniques.routeReason: Plain text; EchoWord covers the stacked echo; the word erase and rebuild is a per-word visibility schedule.

evidence: visuals/a1/p03-echo-card.jpg F189-F201 one word per frame

sound.note: Onsets 28 ms and 16 ms from the two card cuts (7.012, 24.056 s); audio.json holds 132 onsets in 39 s (about 3.4 a second), so an onset within 50 ms of any time is near chance (about a third); tempo confidence 0.074 rules out a beat grid.
